result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy host values verbatim via raw SQL ('INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)'), bypassing the model's before_validation scheme-trimming. Meanwhile record_for_host matches with exact equality ('where("lower(host) = ?", host).first') against uri.host. The deleted spec ('works with a http host' with embeddable_hosts = 'http://eviltrout.com') proves scheme-prefixed entries were a supported legacy form, so migrated rows like 'https://example.com' will never match 'example.com', silently breaking embedding post-upgrade.

judged_text: The migration copies host values verbatim from the old setting, but the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http(s)://` prefixes before matching while the new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored string with exact equality against `uri.host`. Sites whose `embeddable_hosts` setting contained scheme-prefixed entries (a form the old matcher explicitly supported, per the deleted 'works with a http host' spec) get rows stored as `https://example.com`, which never equal `example.com` — their embedding silently stops working after upgrade with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` inserts old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` entries verbatim via raw SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) and thus bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. The new runtime check `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the referer/url and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, which will never match rows stored as `http://example.com` or `https://example.com/123`. The diff also removed the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` logic/specs that explicitly supported scheme-prefixed entries, so upgrades from such configurations can silently break embedding.
